Representative_Docs: ["Misdiagnosed as a child with ADHD. But the more I think about it, and the way my life was, everything points to autism.. I m42 was diagnosed in the late 80s with ADHD. At the time the autism diagnosis was only for people who we would call now low functioning. The nonverbal types. But I never felt like the ADHD diagnosis was correct. My parents put me on Ritalin but I never felt like it worked, I always felt the same. I have no reason to mistrust my parents so I just went with it, trust the process. Eventually in high school they said I grew out of it, but even after I stop the medicine I was still the same. But now that I look back on my life I think the signs are there. I never really had friends growing up, still don't. I always had one or two neighborhood friends but I was never part of a friend group at school. I saw them everywhere but I never fit in. Nobody ever invited me anywhere or asked me to hang out. Yes I'm an introvert but looking back now I see it was more than that. If a professional analyzed my school and tried to pick out who they thought would become a school shooter, I would be at the top of the list. But I was never violent or a troublemaker, just kept to myself. I have always been socially awkward. But at the time I thought everyone was like that. I have always been hyper focused with my interests. I know way too much about Power Rangers and Gundam, that's what I was into in college and high school. Some people would say I made it my personality. Also a few things like Star Wars and Star Trek I am way too into. I like most nerdy interests, but there are a few I am hyper obsessed with. I thought I was just part of a fandom but I realize most of my behavior was way more than just being a fan. I did join an anime club in college but even among them I was an outsider. Because I enjoyed things that were different than what they liked. Even when I was into video games I would focus on just one or two and complete that. Again, just thought that was normal. Even now I have a hard time finding new shows to watch. I just have the same ones on repeat. Change makes me very uncomfortable. I like things the way they are especially if they work for me. I don't like my room rearranged or things moved around. Part of that is my disability. I do have MS and it affected everything below my waist as well as dexterity. So not changing is also practical because I am limited. But I've always been like that. I do except change and I work with it but it makes me uncomfortable. I know there's more I just didn't go into detail. Things like the interest I have go against what is typically seen as popular. I enjoy Arby's, Star Wars episode three is my favorite, certain anime titles that are seen as the best don't interest me. I did have my doctor put in a consult to see an autism specialist to get screened for it. I just want to make sure that I am on the right path. I've been on antidepressants and anti-anxiety medicine but they never felt like they really helped. No noticeable difference. And I've seen therapists but also no help. Probably because we didn't know what the root cause was. I just thought that my quirks and mannerisms were just personality, and everyone is like this just a little different, but we are all relatively the same. Now I'm seeing that that's not the case. And maybe I can move forward.", 'Autism and getting too into a person, help. My feelings are too intense and I just want to be chill.', 'I am a late diagnosed, latino 37 year old man. "Mean girls" have always been my bullies, and I finally understand why.. Guys like me are not prince charming, we arent the male love interest in a Mindy Kaling show. Im supposed to know my place. Women like my wife have a seat at the table, they arent supposed to be with guys like me. To make matters worse, she isnt even white, and she is a self proclaimed progressive feminist. The entire time I have known her, she is constantly complaining "guys just want sex" and "no one wants to have a serious relationship" and "men are all misogynist" and "all the single guys are red hats" that is a code/dogwhistle I felt bad for her, because i know rejection sucks. I played nice the rest of the night, and her small odd behaviors were more obvious of being rude, mean, dissmisive and ignoring me, the owmer of the house and host. Confirmations: 1. This woman is a narcicist leader of a mean girl group with internalized white supremacy and misogyny. 2. She genuinely hated my existence, because of who i am. 3. She was retaliating because I needed support from the group, and it meant I would get kindness and empathy she didnt think I deserved, and taking attention away from her. 4. She hated how my wife, better than her in everywhere looks/personality/profession chose me to marry and is genuinely happy. 5. It meant she was faced with the reality, guys like me are not what she wants, but can succeed, and she might need to settle for a guy like me if she ever wants a relationship. 6. I never did anything "wrong" all these years. I was being rejected by things I couldnt control. My success and perserverence proves to the shitty people in society that their ideology is flawed, and people like me are deserving of kindness, feiendship, acceptence. I told everyone in the group i will never be around if she is still around. 6 months I still have this boundary. I stopped everything group related with them, instead the individuals I genuinely like I hang out with when it is convinient for me, and as individuals or as a couple. Radical acceptence is, yes I am still responsible for working on myself everyday to be better everyway possible. Representative_Docs: ['Anyone else feels like an unlikely collection of misfortunes?. I was born to be trans, I know some people love to be trans, but it\'s undeniably a thing that makes my life harder; stole years of my life through dysphoria; stops me from even consider moving from a handful of countries; makes a number of aspects of my life way more complicated. Let\'s add to that, born with the widest fucking shoulders in a small boob family. I love my HRT, but it can\'t really do anything to fix That. I guess I\'m at least kinda short. Not to add that I apparently was born to have a very androgen-sensitive scalp. Even with strong antiandrogens my hair is shit, can\'t do much about it at this point. Unsure I could even get a transplant, as my hair is very fine. Born with the shittiest metabolism. No matter how much I trie, even in the best conditions losing weight seems impossible, let alone when I\'m dealing with life being shitty. Have you ever tried to be trans and fat? It\'s not great. Most relationship chances seem to go right out of the window And talking about relationships, you know what sucks? Being born asexual. Not the "tee hee asexuals people can have sex too!"-kind of asexual, but the kind of asexual who genuinely does not understand sexuality or why people would want to engage with it. You know how alienating that is in lgbt communities where everyone seems to be all horny all the time? You know how difficult that makes the pursuit of any romantic relationship? The answer is "a lot". Born with fairly prominent autism. Not bad enough that I can prove support need to the extremely strict system in my country, but bad enough that it makes holding any "unskilled" or public facing job incredibly difficult. And that\'s without even considering that it makes my social life basically nonexistent. Born in a shitty family too, mostly got shouted at and called "lazy" for my autistic trait. Never received an inch of support for it. Multiple doctors floated the possibility I could be autistic as a kid, and my parents just decided to ignore them and keep shouting at me. Additionally born into a Poor family. My father was a mean-spirited musician who always refused to get a real job who I eventually had to cut most contacts with , and my mum just floated from odd job, to odd job. Which functionally means no real support has ever been available for me. Which is not a great combination with my inability to hold most jobs for too long. Genuinelly feels like I spent all my life just being deprived of... everything. Specialized into an industry that\'s now collapsing: The one escape I would have had from this was being able to go to uni and specialize in something that would have given me upward class mobility. Except I had the brilliant idea to specialize in game design. Admittedly the field was booming when I was studying it. But it took me forever to even get my first job due to a number of factors, and now the industry has basically collapsed onto itself, and the chance of getting a job especially in Europe, I guess being born in a non-anglophone country for some things is lucky, not for the job angle though; that specific industry is way smaller here is basically zero. There\'s literally no jobs to apply to. I\'m mega fucked. Born with diabetes running in the family too. Yay. I also have shitty teeth, although that tbf is mostly on me, because before my 20s no one had truly explained to me how to take care of them. You know what comes with shitty teeth? anxiety? yup. Constant money sink? Yup. Big gaps in my mouth in the near future? Unless I get significant amounts of money saved up, yup. I\'m sure I\'m forgetting something but GOD, if it feels like I got a bad roll on anything I could have gotten a bad roll on character creation, It feels so fucking pathetic that my biggest dream has always to be just to have a... normal life. To have a steady income doing something that doesn\'t make me burn-out/have panic attacks. Have normal relationships with people. Not feel like an outsider everywhere I fucking go. Not continuously feel like my body is this ugly and decaying mess. Just be able to be without fear of anxiety. I don\'t think it\'ll ever happen. I don\'t think I\'ll ever be normal, and live a life like I see other people living. I don\'t think I\'ll ever be able to fix myself. And it makes life feel completely worthless sometimes. Sad.', 'Friends demeanour after some time apart at work. Hi there! I joined this group a little while ago as I have a few friends that reckon are somewhere on the spectrum and I wanted some insights on how I can better understand their experience and be a better friend to them. I\'m ADHD 34F myself so I understand to some degree about navigating the world as a neuro divergent person. I have a good friend at work that I\'ve gotten to know over that last 2 years and I\'m fairly certain she\'s ASD or some wonderful variety she says herself that she\'s definitely "something" . Before I arrived at this workplace she tended to keep to herself quite a bit judging from what others in the group said, and sadly she\'d been labelled as being "a bit weird". I decided to hell with those judgements, I wanted to get to know her and over time we\'ve slowly but surely developed a great connection. We make coffees together each morning, we go for lunch once a week to some new place she wants to try which is super fun, and we share many common interests and she\'s a great support to me as I try to finish my doctorate. I\'ve visited her home a couple of times now and hung out on weekends. We\'ve even helped each other with our respective work as we have different expertises. She\'s a wonderful person to have as a friend. The thing is, and this is assuming she is ASD, there are still some behaviours for lack of a better word, that puzzle me a bit, and I\'d like some insight from the community as I don\'t want to make a judgement. Often if I\'m away for some longer amount of time, as I have been recently due to health issues, I\'ll come back and she\'ll be very distant, almost hesitant to engage, even though we\'ve kept in touch a bit over text. This happened today, despite the fact that the time we spent the week prior to me being away, we were very engaged with each other. She\'s often more quiet on Monday\'s as I think she\'s usually trying to get into gear for the week and organising her schedule which makes complete sense, but I don\'t know, today I felt that a bit of a wall was up and when we finally said hello it felt very awkward. I probably looked busy as well in all fairness as I was going to a meeting and organising things. But aside from that hello, she was very much wanting I think, to just be in her own space, and get on with her work and doing your work obviously makes sense! I\'m not asking for advice to change her behaviour, it didn\'t upset me, it\'s not something I even plan on bringing up because in the scheme of things, I understand if someone needs space, it might even be something in her personal life or she\'s just really tired. We\'ve been able to discuss things really well when we\'ve had miscommunications, and she\'s very gracious and supremely mature about it, but this seems like such a minor thing to actually bring up. Its just that I find it puzzling and I was just curious if there\'s anything here that I\'m missing. Is it difficult for some people with ASD to re-engage with friends after some time away? Perhaps it\'s the break in a routine or just knowing how to engage? What would be the best thing for me to do to help? Today I just let her be, but made sure to say goodbye when I left. I figured I\'d see how she\'s going tomorrow and make sure to touch base and ask if she\'s doing ok, but aside from that I\'m not sure what and if I should do anything different. TL:DR After my being away from work for a couple of weeks, my possibly ASD friend was awkward and seemed hesitant to engage with me and our usual routine. Representative_Docs: ['I think I found my music. I’ve always had a weird, on-again, off-again relationship with music. Growing up, there wasn’t any music in the house. It was all talk radio. Same in the car. At age 10, I got laughed at by my class because I listened to the ‘boring radio’ instead of the cool music stations. It’s what my mum had on. As I got older, music slowly crept in. I had a phase of years where I needed music to sleep. My mum would yell from the other room, ‘Turn that music down!’ and wake me up. But the music helped. It was soothing. I’ve never been a ‘song’ person. I don’t remember lyrics. But usually prefer tracks with lyrics. Maybe it’s just the sound of a voice that does something for me - I’m not sure. But now I think I’ve found my music. It’s a track from 1994. 8 minutes, 29 seconds. It has 22 different sentences some only one word . They cover 21 letters of the alphabet. I checked. It’s repetitive, but in a way that builds and shifts. It feels like there is an entire world inside it. I’ve had it on repeat since Friday night. Not literally non-stop - I’ve slept, and had work meetings, and family time. But every other moment? Just this. On repeat. I don’t know how many times I’ve heard it now. I just know I want it to keep going. Part of me wishes I’d found this track back in ‘94. Name: 4_teeth_shower_water_brushing
Representative_Docs: ['Tips for brushing/taking care of teeth!. Now I want to start off by saying I am aware these suggestions will not help everyone. I am putting them here because I know there are several people in this community that struggle with it, and I believe these can help at least some of them. Also, if anyone has other suggestions, I’ll create a comment to add them to. Unfortunately I don’t think you can edit posts on this sub. And lastly I am NOT a dentist. These are just things that I have seen, heard, or tried myself. I am open to corrections. -Get an EXTRA soft toothbrush. The bristles will be so soft and thin you can barely even tell them apart. They’re a bit harder to find, so you may have to buy it online, but they’re so much nicer if you have sensitive teeth/gums. They’re completely different from normal “soft” toothbrushes. -If the flavor of mouthwash/toothpaste bothers you, try a kids one instead. They make lots of non-minty flavors. I personally like bubblegum mouthwash. -if you’re anxious about any of the chemicals in mouthwash/toothpaste, like alcohol, food dye, or fluoride, there are alternatives without them. Kids mouthwash also doesn’t have alcohol in it almost 100% of the time. Just to clarify, I’m not claiming these are dangerous, but there are people who have anxiety, trauma, etc. who may be scared to use them -if brushing your tongue is hard, try a soft bristled tongue scraper. Doesn’t require any toothpaste to use, and is much gentler than the metal ones. For me, I gag when I use a toothbrush on my tongue, but not with this. -if it’s hard to use traditional floss, they make floss picks that have disposable attachments and reusable handles. However, some have mint added to them, so if that bothers you be careful when selecting them. Water picks are also an option, but they can be quite expensive. -if the toothpaste getting goopy around the end of the tube bothers you, consider buying bottled toothpaste. I’m assuming some of the kids toothpaste comes this way also. The bottles are also recyclable unlike toothpaste tubes but you must take the label off first! . Another solution is to get a mess free plastic toothpaste dispenser, but it is an extra purchase and some people don’t want to buy a product that’s completely plastic. There may be some biodegradable/sustainably sourced ones. -if you can only brush once a day, it’s better to brush at night than in the morning. That way, you can get rid of all of the particles that built up during the day while eating. -if you can’t brush at all, try doing just a quick swish of mouthwash to get some of the bacteria out. Be careful though, as traditional toothpastes like Listerine can do more harm than good when used too frequently. If using it often, consider switching to a milder kids toothpaste . -if your teeth are very sensitive, use warm/lukewarm water on your toothbrush instead of cold water. -putting less toothpaste on your brush may help with some sensory issues. Most people actually put way too much. Your toothpaste will also last longer as a bonus. -and most importantly, don’t beat yourself up for not doing it “correctly” or “enough”. It’s better to brush for only 30 seconds, floss once a week, etc. than not do it at all. Trying is plenty. I hope this helps ♥️', "Compassion and advice needed - self care. Hey all, I'm audhd, and have also been diagnosed with bipolar 2, anxiety, and depression. For clarity, I was diagnosed in reverse order. I struggle with self care for a lot of reasons. They range from executive dysfunction, to fatigue from depression and physical health complications, to sensory issues with things like brushing teeth or the feel of water on my skin. Especially that half wet, half dry feeling after. I need to shower. It's been too long. It's been at least a month. I have cleaned myself in other ways. Not showering has historically been both a warning sign that I'm facing a depressive crash AND a trigger for said depressive crashes. But over the last year, i had some health complications heart rate spiking when I'm upright or overheated that made showering incredibly difficult. It became routine to not shower, and I'm struggling to break that routine. Right now, I know a shower would be far simpler and faster than the alternative methods to getting clean that I have at my disposal - wet wipes, dry shampoo, etc. I want to shower. I don't feel clean right now, and I know I would feel so good in the shower and after I'm dry. But the thought of showering feels like a giant heavy weight on my chest that makes it feel hard to do anything. The thought of my alternatives which are really just a stop gap method, but not a long term solution makes me feel grubby and gross. Does anyone have any advice for how to get this weight off me when I need to shower? I do all the things I've been able to find on Google and they don't work. I've done all the things I used to do that worked prior to the health issues, and they aren't working either. And every time in the last two decades that I've spoken to a therapist or counselor, I'm told I have all the coping skills and strategies I need, and they can't help me. Frustrating is far too mild a word here. To some extent they are right... I have a tonne of coping skills and strategies. I've taught myself a lot about mental health in general and spent three decades learning what works for me and what doesn't. It's given me a fantastic understanding of how to utilize the tools at my disposal, but more than that, it's given me enough self understanding to know that those tools are not enough. I need help. I need ideas that I maybe haven't tried if it shows up on the first two pages of Google, I can almost guarantee I've tried it . I need the off the wall, no one but someone as desperate as I am would have ever thought of it, random ancient wisdom that is all but forgotten type ideas. And I need to hear someone tell me that I'm not actually gross or disgusting just because I can't shower or brush my teeth consistently.", "Showering and general hygiene — advice needed. Hello there! I'm someone that struggles MASSIVELY with showers/washing/brushing teeth etc. it's usually many months between each shower, since it's vary rare I leave the house. Afterwards is almost as bad— if not worse than— the shower itself. You're damp, unbearably itchy, feeling wrong in your own skin, things stick to you, damp hair though mine's really short, it's still really unpleasant , little bits of dead skin peeling, you smell wrong.... it's awful. Side note: baths are absolutely off the table for many reasons If anyone has any ideas/advice at all, i'd be massively grateful because this is really impacting everything I do, i'm ashamed to leave the house because I know I smell, the dry skin is horrible, it's all just... not great 😅 tl;dr, I need advice with how to make brushing teeth and taking a shower bearable/manageable. Representative_Docs: ['noise cancelling airpod type earphones?. im not very good at english so i didnt know how to say the caption, im trying to look for well functioning earbud bluetooth headphones, like the small ones that go inside your ear. i use noise cancelling headphones from sony at the moment, they dont cancel everything which is perfect so i can use them at school to block out unnecessary noise but still hear the teacher. however id like to use hats, earmuffs, beanies, headbands etc sometimes and the big headset doesnt really let me do that. my sensory issues are pretty bad when it comes to sound and i despise leaving the house without noise cancelling headphones so i never really get an oportunity to use hats and stuff. any good earbuds?', 'Noise Cancelling Over-ear Headphones for windy conditions. Hi. After being admitted to the psychiatric department last year, I was diagnosed with Autism level one and ADHD. I am suffering from burnout, and have discovered that I’m very sensitive to sound, to the point that the least sound dampening earplugs are necessary for gatherings of more than one other person and myself. Since I found out about my sound sensitivity, I have been saving up for noise cancelling headphones, and I looked at the wiki, but the submissions for the Master post about products for Autistics are fairly old, and since the state of technology is in constant flux, and enshitification sadly is a thing, what was good a year ago is not necessarily good today. Because of that and because I live in a very small, windy, and rainy country, and I think I a, justified in writing a new post asking for advice in my purchase of headphones. So the headphones that I buy should ideally have a balanced sound my old Sennheiser HD600 headphones are still my favourite headphones for quiet indoor environments , and should not become noisy if it is windy, and also be able to take some rain, as rain can come very suddenly here. Of those priorities though, the most important one is that they should not become noisy when it is windy. Where I live, there is no such thing as a completely calm day. Even on our hottest 25 degrees Celsius once or twice a year summer days the least wind speeds we get are 5 m/s, and most days have more wind than that. If the headphones become noisy in wind, there is sadly no point in them. If no such headphones exist, then headphones, where you can easily turn off the noise cancellation, are a must. I would be most appreciative if people with relevant experiences could take time to help guide me to my purchase.', 'i was wondering if anyone here had any suggestions for Loop Earplugs for me, since my post on the loop subreddit isnt getting any traffic :/. so basically, i just found my cheap loops from AGES ago that i lost, and sense one of my music earbuds doesnt hold charge, i need a loop for the left ear so i can work and not hear well atleast not easily hear things in my surroundings, like my parents vaccumming and stuff like other music and talking happening while im trying to focus, as i have my right music earbud in but i get to overwhelmed an distracted by other noise since the left earbud dies fast, and is useless for noise cancelation when dead and not playing music... ive seen stuff like the mute add ons and ive seen the loop quiet series as well as the most intriguing to me, the switch ones, but they are so expensive so im unsure what else would fit in my budget and do well, as i really want to get a new pair entirely due to not having the silicone size options from losing them, to what i stated prior with them not doing jack crap. i literally had these on in both ears all day during a school day and i kid you not i forgot i had them in since they did nothing to block out noise, they are worse than covering my ears with my hands T\\^T. again, i really like the concept of the switch ones, for having multiple noise reduction options instead of having multiple different pairs of earplugs. but they a bit too far out pf my price range so all suggestions welcome! any and all suggestions are much appreciated! thanks for reading! have a great day! <333/p']

Name: 6_food_eat_foods_chicken
Representative_Docs: ['Sensory experience of eating. For those of you with food preferences similar to the autism sampler platter meme/stereotype chicken nuggets, pasta, fries, lots of "bland" and beige foods , what\'s your sensory experience of eating like? I\'ve been realizing recently, that my brain doesn\'t really filter foods as enjoy vs. dislike, but more like safe vs. unsafe/suspicious. Bad texture? Suspicious. Too spiced? Suspicious. More than a few ingredients mixed together, like a soup? Hella suspicious. Baked potato? Safe. Preferred juices? Safe. The right brand/type of dino nugs? Hella safe. -- and on and on I realized that part a little while ago actually, but my more recent realization is I\'m not sure how much I\'m actually tasting my foods. When I eat a safe food, and I try to really be mindful and tune into the sensory experience of eating that thing, it\'s surprisingly difficult. I think what I previously assumed was the feeling of enjoying a food might actually just be enjoying a feeling of relief that I\'m eating a thing without any part of me going oh no oh no oh no. I do know that at some point I got very good at automatically tuning out some sensory information as in being very dissociated from my body and all its feelings , so I\'m guessing this is related to that probably. Does this make sense to anyone else? Are other "picky" eaters good at tasting their foods? Sometimes I think I\'m better at feeling foods than tasting them and that\'s why texture matters so much... Has anyone been successful in building up mindfulness skills around eating? Thanks in advance!', 'How to support potentially autistic kid with very limited safe foods. I\'m an autistic mom and maybe also an "autism mom." My elementary school kid almost certainly has ADHD and the chances of autism seem high based on genetics and several behaviors. They have very few "safe foods" and today they told me they don\'t like one of them anymore. I was very particular and restrictive with my eating habits growing up so I understand and am not judging them, but as a parent I\'m realizing the challenges. I\'m a relatively adventurous eater now, the main catalyst was going to live in a college dorm and the cafeteria usually didn\'t have my safe foods so I ended up branching out out of curiousty and necessity. Basically I\'m wondering how other parents support their kids with restrictive eating patterns? I never shame them but I\'ve seen firsthand from others with similar issues how socially isolating it can be to have limited safe food options, especially as an adult. I\'m struggling to walk the line between helping them explore different foods and getting them only the foods I know they will eat which aren\'t necessarily the healthiest, like fast food chicken nuggets . In particular I\'m getting desperate about their school lunches, their school provides free lunch and I was hoping they would explore the daily offerings even if it wasn\'t chicken nuggets, but I recently found out they\'re basically only eating a bag of chips every day. I would do anything for my child and it seems petty and selfish but I am dreading the prospect of packing a lunch every day as my executive function is basically at its breaking point every day and the idea of one more daily task seems impossible. I\'m open to try OT if needed but am trying to explore other options first. I really hope this isn\'t coming across as ableist, I realize it\'s no more their "fault" than it\'s my fault that I get sensory overwhelm very quickly, etc. I\'d just like to help them navigate the world and maybe have an easier time than I did growing up with food.', "ARFID? Name: 7_stim_stims_stimming_feet
Representative_Docs: ['Who else dances as a stim?. I’m looking for people who also stim this way who can share their experiences. From what I’ve heard from neurodivergent people online, they do not see it as a form of stimming, and Neurotypical people get really confused when I dance like this in public because it is often not “pretty” looking or I do it in odd settings. My experience with music and movement is so strong that a lot of times I can’t help but to move in “weird” ways OR specific hand movements following the music. It definitely feels euphoric in the moment but if I do it in public I am overwhelmed by shame because it’s not seen as normal in daily settings! Personally if I don’t do it in the moment when I feel the need to stim in this way. A lot of energy builds up inside me and I end up having meltdowns or the movements shoot out of me sporadically and often violently. Another way I stim ALL THE TIME is I tap or clench parts of my body to the rhythm of music.', "I get this weird urge. Hi, sorry I’m tired, I’m a high masking, yet also high functioning autistic women, yes? and I experience a kind of urge that's hard to explain– it's not quite stimming and not exactly like a tic, but somewhere in between…? I think it maybe starts with a sound or action that loops in my head repeatedly, and over time, it builds up until I eventually have to say it out loud or do it physically. I can hold it back if I really focus or something, especially in public or during class, but it takes effort and can feel like pressure building up inside ig? It doesn't usually come from stress or emotion I’m pretty sure, it feels random– but I'm still somewhat aware of it happening. It's not something I consciously decide to do, but it's also not completely involuntary. Sometimes I'll try to let it out quietly when the urge is strong to avoid attention. It feels different from my usual stimming. Stimming is often more for comfort or regulation, while this is more like a persistent mental itch or loop that needs to be acted on. It’s really strange and hard to explain, and I’m not quite sure what to call it, as, well, I’m not 100% sure how tics feel, I do not have Tourette syndrome myself, but I’m pretty sure this isn’t how that feels like, but like yk kinda similar, and it’s not stimming I don’t think? like I stim sometimes but I also do/feel this and just like yeah idk how to explain, I just had to put this somewhere. I was curious to see if anyone else feels like this too, I couldn’t find anything about it when searching, which is why I’ve decided to post this. Sorry if this makes no sense, I’m tired and not use to posting on Reddit, I’ll probably delete this soon.", 'Can BFRBs be a form of stimming?. So I\'ve seen some discussion around this topic in comments, but wanted to focus on it soecifically - if you engage in body focused repetitive behaviors BFRBs , do you always or sometimes consider them to be a form of stimming? I have pulled hair and picked at my skin for as long as I can remember. The hair pulling on my head has never been to a noticable extent, but the skin picking definitely can be noticable and often painful after the fact from leaving it irritated. As I\'ve learned more about neurodivergence, I\'ve tried to pay more attention to why I do these things: I\'ve found there are multiple reasons - 1 I\'m under stimulated so I give my hands something to do like finding weird texture hairs to pull or bumps on my skin to pick at, often fairly unconsciously. 2 I\'m overstimulated/overwhelmed and anxious and rubbing or picking at my skin becomes a way to help release or channel anxiety. This will often turn into me picking at my shoulders/neck/face until I have aggravated the skin quite badly because I do it with more intensity during these times. 3 Unlike the previous two situations where the bfrbs are reactive behaviors, sometimes I intentionally pick at my skin with the intent of addressing bumps such as cleaning my face and putting on pimple patches . More recently I\'ve been messing with my lower legs where I get irritated hair follicles sometimes and picking at those with tweezers. In both of these examples, the behaviors are much more conscious and I find the process of engaging in them soothing and satisfying until I take it too far and irritate my skin . It\'s like I can get so zoned in and focused on "fixing" the little imperfections that my brain goes much more quiet than normal, which is definitely nice. So in conclusion, sometimes the BFRBs are to help me regulate, and other times they are actively engaged in because it gives me good feels. Would you consider these to be a form of stimming? Does anyone have a more clinical perspective on this from yourself if you are a therapist for example, or as feedback you\'ve received from therapists or doctors for yourself ? Thanks so much for you thoughts!']

Representative_Docs: ["Chemo Hair. Content/trigger warnings: depression, cancer and chemo. tldr: I used to have thick hair, have thin after chemo, and it's hard to remind myself that surviving cancer/chemo is more important than my stupid hair thickness. When I was a kid, I had cancer and went through Chemo. I had the very typical thick Asian hair. Like, thick enough to need more than one hair tie, no amount of washing ever made it clean, thick with 20 c's, you get the point. My hair did grow back, but it was much thinner than before. Thin enough to see scalp and need sunscreen on my head going forward. Honestly, I was lucky in that not all of my hair fell out, but 90% of it did. Since then, I've taken more time to care for what hair I have left and have fun with it. I chose to no wear wigs or hats because the feeling of something compressing my head can be triggering at times, thanks to needing to cover my head during the winter had cancer during Michigan's winter, t'was BRUTAL . Every few years, I'll grow my hair out, donate it, dye it fun colors, grow it out, chop, grow out the natural, donate, rinse and repeat. I've donated my hair since I was in Kindergarten and I don't plan on stopping. I know what it's like to receive a wig that's your hair color, texture, and length, and it's a special feeling that's hard to explain. Being able to contribute to a kid's joy and identity, as small as it is now, matters to me. It's one of the few things I feel like I can genuinely empathize with. Lore dump over, now for the sad brain time thoughts. I hate how thin my hair is. I've seen a specialist to verify that the follicles are super dead and what I have is what I have forever. I sometimes feel like it's getting thinner and thinner, and there will be nothing left. Sure, I might be bald when I'm old and grey, but not something I want while I'm still in my 20's. I've gotten comments from strangers asking where the rest of my hair is, and sometimes I wonder too. I know I should feel absolutely thankful that I am still alive today, able to continue to donate my hair to kids in need, and still have hair on my head that I can do fun things with. I have moments where this doesn't bother me, or I don't even notice it. My wedding day, I had grown my hair out and wore it down. No extensions, no dye, just my natural hair. And those are some of my favorite pictures of myself as an adult. My hairstylist works literal magic and I forget that I have thin hair. In those moments, I see more than just hair; I see me. But sometimes, the sad voice in my head says surviving wasn't worth the hair loss. Right now, I'm trying to find a therapist who can help, but that wishlist is as long as my hair was thiccc, hahahahaha. I have my supportive hairstylist, spouse, in-laws, family, friends, and coworkers who are just happy that I still exist in their lives, appearance be damned. I just wanted to get this vented out, especially to this community as y'all might understand the hyper fixation portion of it all. Thanks for being here with me. -Niv ❤️🧡💛💚💙💜", 'Big thank you to those who posted their sensory driven haircut success pics here. I don\'t really know what flair to put this under and sorry if this is needless... I\'m just throwing this out there. I wanted to send out a big general THANK YOU to this subreddit over the last few years. I\'d seen several people put up pictures of cutting their hair short chin length and above and how it helped them with their sensory problems. I\'ve had short hair before 2 on the sides and back, little fringe in the front , but grew it out because I subscribed to the idea of "rounder faces with soft features need hair to complement their face"... So I grew it out, and the last 7 years I\'ve been miserable with it. It was fine and thin, I had breakage and oiliness, and no kind of masks, low heat/no heat, shampoos, hair training, did anything to combat the no volume, hair breakage I had. On a windy day, a small gust would undo a ponytail or a claw clip. I would spend hours in the bathroom trying to perfect it. I\'m non-binary, I had long hair growing up but never had it up before, so I was never taught how to put it up, but need to now for jobs. Name: 10_driving_drive_traffic_road
Representative_Docs: ['Anyone Else Hate Suburban Driving? An Autistic Perspective. Fellow autistics, does suburban driving on arterial roads drive you up the wall? The sensory overload is relentless: traffic lights flashing, red light cameras lurking, and intersections where right turns feel like a trap. Lights every few kilometers and gridlocked traffic make me feel like I’m being watched, treated like a kid who can’t be trusted. I’m autistic, and my focus isn’t always sharp, especially at 5am heading to work. Once, I zoned out—not on my phone, which I’d never do—and missed a red light. That double flash cost me a $600 fine and a $1000 deal with a family member to save my license from demerit points. I was livid, not just at the money, but at myself for messing up. The shame hit harder than the fine. Rural driving is my sanctuary. Past Nuriootpa, it’s open roads, a few stop signs, and no soul-crushing traffic lights. Roundabouts keep things smooth, and I can just be me, free from the suburbs’ judgmental glare. Stop signs are clear—I stop, no guesswork. Traffic lights, with their yellow-phase chaos, are sensory torture, forcing stops and starts that scramble my brain. A rural mistake might mean a crash, but it’s honest, not a mailed penalty. Now, I cycle to the train station, then head to the truck yard for rural runs driving my truck. My car’s only for 100km/h roads to flight school—no lights, no stress. City driving? Done. If there’s a traffic light, I’m out. Anyone else feel this way? Rural roads let us breathe and drive without the suburban nightmare. Yellow traffic lights are a nightmare for autistic drivers. The split-second choice—slam the brakes or continue through—feels like a sensory trap. For an autistic brain, this ambiguity spikes anxiety, disrupts focus, and demands instant judgment under pressure. Hesitate, and you risk a red light camera’s $600 fine; misjudge, and you’re kicking yourself for failing. Unlike clear stop signs, yellow lights are a chaotic decision limbo that suburban roads amplify.', "Sometimes I feel like I shouldn't be driving. I know it's a huge privilege to drive but I only do it because it's necessary to get around. It's impossible for me sometimes to drive somewhere new and when driving, the littlest things get to me. When I was 1st start to driving around 2ish years ago, it got so bad that I either cried before or after, if not both. One time I even confused the pedals in the heat of the moment because I was tearing up and rushing to part so I can run into my house but almost drove right into my stepfathers truck. But since I was learning everything, everyone said it was road anxiety and I'll get over it. And yeah, I have to a point but there's many times where I just can't? The other week when I was coming back from work there was a crash that stopped my typical path and I had to pull over 3 times to find a way around and get back on my path again. Not sure if that was a meltdown because it was shirt and sweet so I'll just say it was mild panic with tears. Though if I don't use Google maps and pretend drive to my new local at least three times, I cant drive to anywhere new. I try to avoid it at all cost. There's also being a little distracted, I feel like I'm either not paying attention or too much that everything causes me to panic. There's also a lot of road rules and because of rush hour sometimes, I've almost gotten into an accident multiple times just because the turn lane doesn't always have an arrow. Sudden changes happen a lot and they always get to me. It doesn't help that I have parking spots that I prefer for places I've been before and somehow, IT HAPPENED TWICE TODAY. People keep taking my parking spots, which like I know they don't know... most of the time. Even if the destination is the same, if the path is altered by even a block difference, I drive like a asshole just because I'm panicking. And then no one warns me that they are, in fact, changing the route. It is a little better if I'm prepared for change. Think the only good thing about driving is that I love my little car, and I suppose I can get to other places without help or worrying if it's going to be a time crunch. This is more of a rant to myself, I know many people don't drive for many reasons so I really have no right to complain. But sometimes I wish I was in a place with subway trains for transportation.", 'Mad about an IMO unjust speeding ticket. TW: speeding ticket/ACAB Rant/vent strong language American driving laws I just got my first speeding ticket and I’m not necessarily mad about it, but I am mad about the situation that got me a speeding ticket. Situation: two lane divided highway on a Saturday evening when it’s still bright out and the traffic is practically deserted; long stretches of road with one to zero cars in the lane. So I’m cruising above the speed limit because no one is around me and who the hell cares if there’s no one else around, aside from a car every now and then. Apparently edging 90mph when hardly anyone is around is rewarded with a bastard cop too happy to give out a ticket for “speeding and reckless driving.” Again, not mad at the ticket, per se, but mad at the injustice of the ticket. I am a good driver. I just like to go fast, and I don’t like being on congested highways. I’ve had my license for 15 years and I’ve never gotten a speeding ticket and never been in a crash. I’m usually in the right lane following the speed of the other cars around me, and if they’re going stupid-slow, I get in the left lane and pass them the correct way, using my signal! Granted, I’ve never edged so far up to 90, but again, who the hell cares on a deserted highway? Back to the situation, I was following a car that I had JUST caught up to and was slowing down. I don\'t think I was following too closely, and I didn\'t even notice the fucking COP TAILGATING ME until I saw his lights go on. But in my speedster mind, I go around on the left of the slow car and then signal back over when I\'m a considerable distance away from the slowpoke to cruise at my faster speed, and apparently, that\'s considered "reckless driving." So here’s where my “autistic sense of justice” comes into play: I’ve seen drivers do WAY worse than I did on a congested interstate and you rarely see them get pulled over for doing way more stupid and reckless behavior. Representative_Docs: ['Overestimating friendships?. My best friend is getting married and has not asked me to be a bridesmaid. Some of them family, so at first I thought she was doing a family only bridal party but then starting talking about whether to ask two women she works with. To be honest, I\'ve barely heard her speak about these two women at all, and only then when discussing work and workplace drama. We\'ve known each other for a decade and have lived together for several years before finding partners. Any time we spend time together we\'ll hang out for a whole day and we\'d see each other typically once or twice a month. Her wedding is also on my 30th birthday - she apologized for this when she told me the date but said basically it was their favourite venue and it was the only date available that year. I understand this and told her I\'d love to spend my day celebrating her wedding regardless of the date. Even if I\'m a little sad to not be spending the day exactly how I want. My gf and I were planning to do a trip to some of America\'s national parks for my 30th however that plan has changed due to the political instability in the US and overall hostility towards queer and trans people. But even before that I had said thank you for telling me the date in advance of the save the dates, because I would have been planning to be on a trip then otherwise I\'m now starting to wonder if I\'ve overestimated the friendship. On one hand, I\'m queer and have been in a relationship for almost the entire time I\'ve known her, and have little interest in getting married myself. I\'ve always said if it happens it happens, but it\'s never been a "goal" of mine. So maybe she thinks I wouldn\'t be interested in participating in such a heteronormative affair. Being a bridesmaid does not particularly appeal to me in terms of having to mask extra, get my photo taken and spend the day with the rest of the bridal party rather than my spouse. However I had hoped I would be asked because I know how important getting married is to her, and I had thought we were close friends. Regardless, it\'s made me question the if she regards me with the same level of closeness that I regard her. I\'m feeling quite sad about this now because overestimating friendships is something I have done in the past and only realized when the other person has not been there for me when I needed them family disowned for being queer etc or has treated me poorly outright. I suppose I am posting to get some advice on the situation and commiseration if you\'ve ever been in this sorr of situation.', 'I\'m engaged but don\'t have any friends I ask about wedding stuff. Tdlr: I want to get married and don\'t know how to plan it. Please tell me about your non traditional weddings and your thoughts about your own wedding!! So I got engaged last year we both decided, it wasn\'t a surprise and we\'ve decided on a month later next year. My boyfriend is probably ND but not to the same extent as me and we talk about everything and anything. Except I am definitely more into this wedding stuff than he is and I can feel myself getting excited about it but I am also super conflicted about it. We\'re not religious, we have a house together, and I live far away from my family, so from a practical standpoint getting married is important for legal rights and access if something happens to one of us. But then I also want to get married because you\'re "supposed to" I guess. I feel this big pressure from society to do something good and fit in, a society I have already struggled to fit into for so long. But on the other side of it, I don\'t want to have a traditional wedding. I don\'t want to get married in front of anything because that\'s mortifying. So we have decided to elope and have a party a few days later. I don\'t have any close female friends or even enough that I\'d want a bridal party. I know this to be true but there\'s a part of me that left out little girl in school who still feels sad that I don\'t have the choice. I feel embarrassed that I have a small family and only want to invite friends that I talk to on a regular basis. So I\'m embarrassed that my guest list is only 50 people at a push. And then when it comes to the actual planning. I have no desire to spend £4000+ on just one day. I just want to hire a hall and have a party and dance with my friends. But apparently even 10k is considered a "cheap" wedding!! I\'m happy to do my own decorations, hire a food truck, and have a phone attached to some speakers although I\'d love a band, I know that\'s for rich people . And then comes the practical questions. When do invitations go out? How far in advance do you book a venue? When do you get a dress? How do you decide on and plan on activities? Will people think I\'m lame if I don\'t have 100 friends? I could invite 100 people but I don\'t like the idea of inviting people who aren\'t in my close circle.', "How could I celebrate my birthday/bon voyage in a way that feels authentic while starting my unmasking journey?. Hi everyone! My birthday is coming up on June 14th, and it’s also kind of a bon voyage celebration before I travel for a few months. Recently, I’ve been doing some deeper self-reflection, with my therapist, we strongly suspect I’m autistic. I’m trying to begin an unmasking journey, which for me means leaning into what I ACTUALLY want to do, rather than doing what’s expected of me or what other people want. Every year since I was 16, I've hosted a birthday party, and it’s usually something my friends look forward to. I’ve already sent a 'save the date' to about 15 friends all from different social circles, the biggest group is 4 people , and a few have already started asking me what the plan is. There’s definitely an expectation that I’ll do something, and when I’ve hinted I might not, I keep hearing “You’ll regret it!” or gentle nudges to still go ahead. The thing is, I’m just not sure I’m feeling it this year. I’ve been trying to drink less in social settings to get to know my true personality better, and the stress of planning a party, especially mixing friend groups I've recently hated the fact that I mix my friend groups, it may be a jealousy thing??? , feels more draining than exciting. I’ve also had a couple of people cancel last minute in the past, I usually take it personally, which makes it harder to feel excited. So I’m conflicted. On one hand, I could go ahead with the party, it is fun in the moment and it would mean I get to celebrate with everyone at once. But on the other hand, I want to respect where I’m at and maybe explore something different that feels closer to what I need right now. I just dont know what that different is in this moment Has anyone else been in a similar place? Where you’ve wanted to break tradition and celebrate in a new, more authentic way? Any ideas for things I could do that still feel meaningful without the pressure of a full blown party? Just to be clear, I DO want to do something, but I dont know if a party with all my friends together drinking is what I want. Maybe I'm overthinking this.... Would really appreciate any advice or perspective on how to navigate this"]

Name: 14_loud_sound_noises_noise
Representative_Docs: ["Best earplugs to block constant 24/7 droning noise from my neighbor's swamp cooler. Hello friends. This post is part seeking advice, part rant. I live in an apartment building with no AC in the desert. It gets hot. Every unit has a ceiling swamp cooler which can bring the temp from 100 to 85 if you're lucky. It turns on in April and turns off in October. My downstairs neighbor keeps hers on the entire time, 24/7, for the 6 months it's hooked up and running. No breaks, even when she's at work or on vacation. Since her ceiling is connected to my floor, it makes my entire apartment drone and vibrate loudly. It turned on today and I cried, lol. It's my third summer putting up with this and I'm just not excited about it. Also, it doesn't even work if you keep it on 24/7! It only works for about an hour and then you have to turn it off for at least 30 minutes so it can reset! And this downstairs neighbor also likes to smoke cigarettes indoors, which is against the rules of the lease, and leave her laundry in the single machine shared by the entire building for 24+ hours 🙃 I'm in the market for comfortable and effective noise-cancelling earplugs that can bring me some quiet when I need a break from the never-ending drone. Ideally it would be nice to still be able to hear things close to me, like my partner's voice, but blocking out the swamp cooler is the priority. Comment your recommendations! Thank you so much 💕", "Sound sensitivity makes me feel like a bad neighbor. Of all my sensory sensitivities, sound is the one that has the most impact on me. Idk if I just live in an extra noisy neighborhood, or if I'm just that sensitive, but I get so overwhelmed and subsequently cranky and subsequently ragey at the level of noise where I live. I feel like there is almost always a power tool going on for extended periods. There is almost always at least one dog barking constantly. My neighbor's laundry room is near my bedroom window, so I can hear their machine, and they do laundry all freaking day, until 10 or 11pm sometimes. How does one household have so much laundry?!? Why do they do it so late!?! I can't stop thinking about it. Loud ass motorcycles tearing down the street that sets off car alarms. Bone rattling bass from people's speakers. Helicopters circling. Conversations between loud talkers that seem to go on forever. Children playing outside and shouting. The thing is, I know these are all normal sounds for an urban neighborhood, and are just people living their lives. I know I'm the one with the problem, not them. But it makes me feel really bitter and irritated with my whole neighborhood. I don't want to be the cranky old lady on the street who hates everyone, but this is what my sound sensitivities lead to. Yes, I have earplugs for when I really need, but I don't like wearing them all the time bc - surprise - sensory issues. And I also get angry at the idea of even having to wear ear plugs inside my own home where I am supposed to have control over my environment. UGGHH. How do y'all cope with sound sensitivities when the stimulus is constant? How do you not become riddled with hate? How do you not have constant meltdowns?", 'Morning anger and bird-hatred. I am 49 and was recently identified by an autism specialist as being on the spectrum. No formal diagnosis, but we did several weeks of behavioral exercises and he’s certain - and based on what I’m learning, it explains 99% of why I struggle with things that others do not . Does anyone else deal with intense anger for the first 10-30 minutes of the day after being woken up by their alarm and HATING “morning sounds” like the alarm itself and birds chirping? If my alarm was a person, I would want to shoot it in the head. I have to switch alarm ring tones every few weeks because it will get to a point that the alarm sound will trigger an excess of “anger-at-the-world-for-making-me-get-up-and-conform-to-social-expectations.” I ran out of new alarm tones a long time ago, so I am stuck with all the ones that make me angry, although some make me slightly less angry than others. I also HATE bird sounds. I have lived a lot of places, but become extremely attuned to birds chirping when I am “forced” to wake up. It’s so intense that for 5-10 minutes, I wish that all birds everywhere in the whole world would simultaneously drop dead. Once I get accustomed to the morning bird sounds often a particular place, I just feel even angrier at them in the morning because they “trigger” me. I also feel angry at car sounds, light, etc. But I am not an angry person - I hate feeling angry because it’s physically/mentally so unpleasant. But for the first 30 minutes of the day it’s like I am an entirely different person. I get up an hour early every day so I can “adjust” from hatred-at-world and feel normal - but it’s more than “adjustment,” I feel like a have a totally different brain in the morning. It doesn’t help that I also intellectually hate the fact that we all have to conform to capitalist scheduling. After I have transitioned to “awake,” all of my bird genocide fantasies disappear- because I actually REALLY like birds. Birds are super cool! I have always struggled to make sense of why/how I feel so radically inconsistent in the morning and about birds. I think everyone probably hates alarms - although my alarm hatred is on the extreme end. But birds? Does any of this sound like spectrum stuff? There are a million things I would change about myself if I could, but how I feel for the first 30 minutes of the day would be 1.']

Representative_Docs: ['What do you do for skincare?. Hi first time poster here and not much of a Reddit user, so sorry if there are already threads like this. I’ve never had a skincare routine because of a pretty bad sensory aversion to things on my skin, with creams especially really making me freak out. My main needs are an spf ideally 50+ as I’m very pale lol , face cleanser/moisturiser I can use after shaving as my skin gets very irritated, and body oils for dry skin/dermatitis that I could ideally rinse off not long after putting them on. I’ve tried a lot of different products but pretty much everything makes me freak out to the point of scratching my skin so much I might as well have used nothing. There are a few water based products I’ve found that don’t cause me as many issues like neutrogena water based stuff, but they all feel a bit too expensive for how little you get and how much they actually do. The one product I’ve used that has worked and hasn’t given me too many issues is the aveeno shower cleansing oil as I can put it on and rinse it off before it causes me too much stress, but they’ve recently encountered some supply issues and I can’t find it anywhere 🫠 What would you guys recommend? Hi there, as already stated in the caption, I’m really looking for sensory friendly skincare solutions. Has anyone here tried dealing with this successfully?', 'Smell sensitivity tips?. Of all my senses, smell is the most intense for me and the one that I get overwhelmed by most frequently. Over a decade ago I started phasing scented things out of my life, so now I use only unscented everything, with exceptions for a few essential oil scents that I can handle as long as they aren\'t too strong. Unfortunately this means I\'m used to being in a scent-free environment, so when I do have to be around scented products or other strong smells, it\'s even harder to cope. Honestly feel marginally jealous of people who are most sensitive to sound or light not at ALL to minimize your struggles - I wouldn\'t wish them on anyone just because there are actual well-accepted and accessible tools to help mitigate those sensitivities. Name: 19_hot_heat_temperature_cold
Representative_Docs: ["how do you guys deal with physical effects of overstimulation?. so the past couple years i've been living pretty isolated, as a consequence of some mental health problems mixed with the fact i am so easily overstimulated. lately i'm trying to be out and about more and i've been going on walks, which i really enjoy aside from the fact that after even only half an hour i will have a severe headache that leaves me in pain for hours even once i'm home. i don't think it's a good idea to take pain killers every time that happens, because i would be taking them very often. how do other people manage this? something else i really struggle with is heat, as i'm sure many others here do. it's physically excruciating for me when it's hot, the sun itself feels like it's actively burning my skin and i get the feeling like i'm being poked with needles everywhere. i sweat so easily and then the sensation of sweat on my body and my clothes sticking to me just makes me want to take everything off and lay on the floor making sure nothing is touching my skin. any tips would be appreciated!", 'Does your autism cause thermoregulation issues?. I have always had temperature sensitivities. As a kid, me being constantly cold was a greater issue to the point where when my mom was dying one of the last things she said to me was, “You were always so cold… all the time.” . During COVID I was sent home from work a lab for 6 months because I spiked a low fever essentially every day, and my doctor had to prove my temperature wasn’t associated with any infections. As an adult, I’m better at managing cold… I ALWAYS have extra layers or blankets. But heat and sweating is a real issue. It basically takes only the slightest bit of physical activity, or stress with even less activity and I’m so hot I feel like I can’t function and sweat is running in rivers down my back etc. It’s obscene. My partner and I have a deal where I never vacuum because I get too hot. It’s impacting me so much I’m starting to be willing to do less and less because of how hot and uncomfortable I get. You guys sweaty and hot for seemingly no reason? Is there anything that can be done? Aside from like fans and ice packs… both of which I have many. Note: I even had my doctor check if I was in early menopause or something. Nope.', 'Driving in the heat is so overstimulating and awful. It’s starting to feel like summer here in the South and driving is becoming worse and worse I decided to hike in the middle of the day with a heat index of over 100F, and I was already hot and sweaty when returning to the car. That sticky feeling. The feeling of even one hair touching my face. The feeling of sweat making clothes more coarse and irritating. Or dirt sticking to me. The feeling of irritability and rage that comes from temperature being out of whack. Then I get in the car. It’s a greenhouse. I turn on the AC. Temporary relief. It cools down too quickly, even on the lowest setting. The parts of my body in the path of the AC get cold and that’s overstimulating. The parts outside the path of the AC get too hot because greenhouse effect. Everything is sticky. I felt everything. My patience dropped. The patience of other drivers is thin in the heat, too. I worried more about dodging the rage of an overheated suburban man in a 6000 pound death machine. Ah, I love summer.']
